question.text: How can photochemical smog be controlled?

options.text: By using catalytic converters in the automobiles/industry

solution.text: Catalytic converters force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>CO</mi></math> and incompletely combusted hydrocarbons to react with a metal catalyst, typically platinum, to produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo> </mo></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math>. Additionally, catalytic converters reduce nitrogen oxides from exhaust gases into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, eliminating the cycle of ozone formation.
